Where the project actually stands
I read dump.txt and claude-terminal.txt before writing anything. Two things worth stating up front:

M5 is closed and the tree is green. Your last sweep reported total: 934, failed: 0, succeeded: 919, skipped: 15 with a clean run.sh --smoke and a healthy --containers-only. The event explorer landed. §19's M5 line is fully discharged.
The /account/enroll-totp 500 in my notes is stale — EnrollTotp.razor is in the tree, the suite is green, and nothing in the terminal log reproduces it. I've treated it as resolved rather than re-litigating it.
So the next step is M6, and its first slice is CI — §16.4, "GitHub Actions — build, unit, integration (service container PostgreSQL), E2E (compose), publish image on tag." I picked CI over the Playwright matrix deliberately: your hardest constraint is that I write C# I cannot compile, and CI is the thing that closes that loop without you in it.

The slice as it stands
New (5): .github/workflows/ci.yml (shell lint · strict Release build + full suite · boot-smoke, which builds the Containerfile and boots the image against real PostgreSQL until /healthz/ready answers 200 — the only gate that catches migration and composition-root failures), .github/workflows/release.yml (calls ci.yml via workflow_call, then pushes to GHCR on v*), .github/dependabot.yml, scripts/ci_local.sh, docs/_append/BUILD_PROGRESS-m6-slice-1.md.

Edited (5): Directory.Build.props (TreatWarningsAsErrors true only under ContinuousIntegrationBuild, with NU1901–NU1904 exempt — this finally answers the "flip to true once the first green build is established" note the file has carried since M1), tests/MyRestaurant.DataAccess.Tests/Sittings/SittingRecordReadsTests.cs (the xUnit2031 warning at line 354, which strict CI would otherwise fail on), README.md, docs/OPERATIONS.md (new §14), _CHANGES.md.

Files to delete: none.

Two design notes: CI does not use compose.yaml, because the :U volume suffix is Podman-specific and Docker Compose rejects it — a service container plus one docker run --network host is the same topology without that fight. And the release image is linux/amd64 only; arm64 under QEMU would emulate a full dotnet publish and time out, so it wants a cross-compiled -r linux-arm64 Containerfile change rather than a workflow line.

Verification I ran on the archive itself
I extracted the tarball over a pristine copy of your tree (rebuilt from dump.txt, hash-verified) and diffed. Result: exactly those 10 paths, zero collateral changes. Directory.Build.props parses as well-formed XML, all three workflow YAMLs parse, and scripts/ci_local.sh is clean under bash -n and shellcheck --severity=style.

The SittingRecordReadsTests.cs diff is literally 354c354 — nothing else in that 28 KB file moved.

Two notes worth reading before you run it
dotnet test should still say 934 / 919 / 15. The xUnit2031 fix changes an assertion's form, not its meaning or its count. If the total moves, something else moved with it.

bash scripts/ci_local.sh is the real check here — it is the first thing in this repository's history to run the strict build (Release + warnings-as-errors). If it goes red on a warning your Debug builds never showed, that is the gate working rather than a defect; fix it or add the code to WarningsNotAsErrors with a comment. That's the one thing I couldn't verify without an SDK.

Then push and watch the Actions tab — roughly shell-scripts under a minute, build-and-test 5–8 (no NuGet cache on the first run), boot-smoke 4–7. Worth cutting v0.6.0 once while it's fresh, to prove the release path before it matters.

Where M6 stands
Three of §19's six M6 items shipped inside earlier milestones (cloudflared profile, quick-tunnel script, OPERATIONS runbooks). With CI landed, two remain: the Playwright harness and an executable backup/restore drill.

Next slice is the harness — a stack fixture, a browser context, a virtual authenticator, a controllable clock — carrying scenarios 1, 13 and 14, because the passkey and token-window plumbing they need is what the other twelve are waiting on.

One thing I'd flag: my notes said M2 was blocked on a 500 at /account/enroll-totp. Your green sweep and the current tree say otherwise, so I treated it as closed. If it's still there, that jumps the queue.
